Chemicals Firm Unveils Innovative Additive at Antwerp Event

Antwerp—Belgium’s chemicals industry saw the launch of a new polymer additive yesterday, as Kynelix NV announced its latest product at a gathering of sector leaders and researchers. The additive, branded as Kynelene, is designed to enhance the durability and recyclability of industrial plastics, and is set to be produced at Kynelix’s facility in the Port of Antwerp.

Speaking at the event, Kynelix CEO Veerle D’Hondt highlighted the company’s commitment to sustainability: “With Kynelene, we aim to support our customers in meeting stringent EU recycling targets while offering performance benefits. This launch is the result of three years of R&D and collaboration with our partners.”

Industry observers noted that the Belgian chemicals sector, which employs nearly 90,000 people and accounts for 17% of the country’s exports according to Essencia, the national chemicals federation, continues to prioritize innovation amid shifting regulatory demands. “There is strong momentum in Belgium for greener solutions,” said Tom Van Loon, an analyst at ChemMarkets. “Firms are investing in circular economy technologies, and Kynelene fits this trend well.”

Kynelix expects Kynelene to enter commercial production by September, with initial deliveries to Belgian and Dutch plastics manufacturers. The company forecasts that the additive will enable plastics to retain mechanical properties after recycling, a key concern for packaging and automotive suppliers.

The launch was welcomed by the Flemish Innovation Agency, which praised the project’s contribution to regional competitiveness and environmental goals.
